typical_topologies_ahb: Single-Manager AHB-Lite: one Manager + one centralized decoder + one Subordinate-to-Manager multiplexor + N Subordinates (Figure 1-1).
Multi-Manager AHB: interconnect provides arbitration and routing; see ARM DVI 0045 Multi-layer AHB Technical Overview.
Multi-layer AHB: multiple parallel Manager-Subordinate paths; each layer is effectively a separate AHB-Lite single-Manager bus.
typical_topologies_apb: Single APB bridge (Manager) + multiple APB peripherals (Subordinates) sharing PADDR / PWRITE / PWDATA / PENABLE; per-peripheral PSELx.
An AHB-to-APB or AXI-to-APB bridge connects the high-performance system bus to the peripheral bus.

interconnect_role_ahb.decoder: Generates one HSELx per Subordinate by decoding the upper address bits. Minimum decode granularity = 1KB. Decoder also drives the multiplexor control (retimed to data phase).
interconnect_role_ahb.multiplexor: Routes HRDATA + HRESP + HREADYOUT (+ HEXOKAY when AHB5) from the selected Subordinate back to the Manager. Combines all HREADYOUTs into the single HREADY broadcast.
interconnect_role_ahb.default_slave: If memory map incomplete, an additional default Subordinate must be implemented to return ERROR for NONSEQ/SEQ to unmapped addresses and zero-wait OKAY for IDLE/BUSY.
interconnect_role_ahb.multi_manager: Multi-Manager systems require an interconnect with arbitration; details outside the scope of the AHB spec itself.

interconnect_role_apb.bridge: The APB Manager. Decodes upstream (AHB / AXI) accesses into APB transfers, generates PSELx per peripheral, drives PADDR/PWRITE/PSELx/PENABLE/PWDATA/PSTRB/PPROT, captures PRDATA, and maps PSLVERR back to the upstream protocol's error response.
interconnect_role_apb.psel_routing: Bridge decodes upper PADDR bits to generate the appropriate single PSELx per transfer.

interconnect_rules_ahb: Decoder must drive HSELx during the address phase (same cycle as the address and other control signals for non-IDLE transfers).
HSELx may be asserted or deasserted for IDLE transfers (Section 2.4).
Multiplexor control signals must be retimed to the data phase (Section 4.2).
A single centralized decoder is required in implementations that use two or more Subordinates.
A single centralized multiplexor is required in implementations that use two or more Subordinates.
Default Subordinate returns ERROR for NONSEQ/SEQ to undecoded addresses, zero-wait OKAY for IDLE/BUSY.
Multiple HSELx may be asserted for a single Subordinate (Section 4.2.2 — Multiple Subordinate select pattern) to provide multiple logical interfaces.
HREADY is computed by combining all Subordinate HREADYOUTs.
Generic interconnect may offer AHB as one of several interface options (AXI / APB other choices).
interconnect_rules_apb: Bridge generates one PSELx per peripheral by address decode.
Only one PSELx asserted per transfer.
Bridge holds PADDR, PWRITE, PSELx, PENABLE, PWDATA, PSTRB, PPROT stable while PREADY=0 (Subordinate inserting wait states).
AHB-to-APB bridge appears as an AHB Subordinate; PSLVERR maps to HRESP=ERROR.
AXI-to-APB bridge: PSLVERR maps to RRESP/BRESP = SLVERR (RRESP[1] or BRESP[1]).
Peripherals that do not support PSLVERR have their PSLVERR input to the bridge tied LOW.

id_routing_ahb.description: Single-Manager AHB-Lite has no ID concept (only one Manager). Multi-Manager AHB5 uses HMASTER as a Manager identifier; the interconnect is responsible for modifying HMASTER from each Manager port to ensure global uniqueness across the system.
id_routing_ahb.implication: HMASTER_WIDTH at the interconnect ingress (per Manager port) must accommodate all Manager IDs in the system.

guaranteed: All beats of a burst are presented to the same Subordinate in HBURST-defined order.
Single-Manager AHB-Lite: strict request order = response order (single outstanding).
Locked sequences (HMASTLOCK=1) are not interrupted by other Managers (multi-Manager only).
Strict in-order on a single APB bus (one bridge, one outstanding transfer).
not_guaranteed: Ordering across multiple APB busses fed by independent bridges.

memory_vs_peripheral_regions.ahb_memory_subordinate: Maps to a memory region; handles all bursts/sizes correctly.
memory_vs_peripheral_regions.ahb_peripheral_subordinate: Typically connected via an AHB-to-APB bridge; APB peripheral behaviour governed by APB protocol.
memory_vs_peripheral_regions.apb_peripheral_region: PADDR-mapped peripheral register set; one PSELx per logical peripheral.

slave_classification_ahb.Memory_Subordinate: Handles all AHB transaction types; uses HREADYOUT to insert wait states for slow memory.
slave_classification_ahb.Peripheral_Subordinate: Often APB peripheral behind an AHB-to-APB bridge.
slave_classification_ahb.Default_Subordinate: ERROR for NONSEQ/SEQ at unmapped addresses; zero-wait OKAY for IDLE/BUSY.

slave_classification_apb.Memory_mapped_peripheral: Standard APB peripheral; uses PREADY to extend ACCESS phase if needed.
slave_classification_apb.Fixed_two_cycle_peripheral: PREADY tied HIGH; every transfer completes in exactly 2 PCLK cycles.
slave_classification_apb.PSLVERR_supporting: Drives PSLVERR=1 in the cycle PREADY=1 to indicate failure.
slave_classification_apb.Non_PSLVERR_supporting: PSLVERR input to the bridge tied LOW.

evidence.spec_section: 1.1 About the protocol — Interconnect / Decoder / Multiplexor
evidence.quote: A single Manager AHB system design with the AHB Manager and three AHB Subordinates. The bus interconnect logic consists of one address decoder and a Subordinate-to-Manager multiplexor.

Interconnect / Address decoding / Read data and response multiplexor / Interconnect with AHB interfaces. Generic interconnect products can offer AHB as an interface option, among others such as AMBA AXI or AMBA APB.

Minimum address space 1KB on 1KB boundary. Default Subordinate provides ERROR for NONSEQ/SEQ to undecoded addresses, zero-wait OKAY for IDLE/BUSY. Multiple HSELx may be asserted for a single Subordinate to provide multiple logical interfaces.
HMASTER may be modified by the interconnect to ensure each Manager has a globally unique ID.
PSELx — APB bridge generates this signal to each peripheral bus slave; one PSELx per slave.
AHB-to-APB: PSLVERR -> HRESP=ERROR (HRESP[0]). AXI-to-APB: PSLVERR -> RRESP/BRESP = SLVERR (RRESP[1] / BRESP[1]).
